_comment: The texts of Call of Duty: Black Ops's README that are its own (tools/title_readme.py has the common ones).
pitch: It starts from a recompilation of the campaign and Zombies executable with ReXGlue v0.10.0, built directly on Any360 from its first day: the fifth title the toolkit runs, and the first ported with nothing written for it in Any360 but the system calls no title before it used.
own_copy: You need your own copy of the game (the USA/Europe disc, title 41560855); the recompiled C++ is generated on your machine from your disc's `default.xex`.

state.recompiled: `default.xex` (the campaign and Zombies) fully translated (18,886 functions; the ones reached only through pointers are declared in [config/](config/)); `default_mp.xex`, the multiplayer, is not recompiled yet
state.library: not started: the C runtime and XDK functions Any360 already has for the other titles are to be found in this executable and checked in game before they are bound
state.game: not started (the count is in the table above)

run: `--any360_gpu=true` draws the game through `any360::gfx`; `--any360_sys_groups` puts the Xbox system calls on `any360::sys`. Without them the game runs on ReXGlue's runtime, as recompiled.
build: Windows, Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ and Clang tools, an install of the ReXGlue SDK v0.10.0 (`-Sdk`, the folder with `bin\rexglue.exe`, `include\` and `lib\`) and an [Any360](https://github.com/GaetanVigner/Any360) checkout (`-Any360`).
1. Extract your disc into `game\` (for example with [extract-xiso](https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso)), so that `game\default.xex` exists.
4. Run `out\build\codbo.exe`. It finds `game\` next to itself or in the repository; logs are written to `out\build\logs\`.

Code reached only through vtables or data pointers is invisible to the codegen: [tools/find-missing-functions.py](tools/find-missing-functions.py) scans the decrypted image (`out\image\default_image.bin`) for such targets and writes them to [config/discovered-functions.toml](config/discovered-functions.toml); the ones only a run of the game reveals are in [config/overrides.toml](config/overrides.toml).
credits: Call of Duty: Black Ops by Treyarch, published by Activision (2010).
legal: An unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Activision or Treyarch. It is not a replacement for the game: you still need to own a copy, and nothing of the game is in this repository.
